newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine cash rule seen cutting banks' cash inflow.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine cash rule seen cutting banks' cash inflow.

text.p: An order from Ukraine's central bank allowing commercial banks to seize money from hard currency accounts of debtor firms will boost barter trade and cut banks' cash inflows, a senior commercial banker said.

"The reaction of enterprises in our region has been clear: we will barter, the same thing we did earlier to save ourselves from paying taxes," Anatoly Volok, president of Kharkov's Region Bank told a news conference.
He said increased use of barter would lead to a large drop in cash inflow to banks.
Many Ukrainian enterprises owe hryvnia to creditors like the tax inspection department, energy companies, workers, and other entities.
But officials say some deposit cash in hard currency accounts and claim they do not have hryvnia to pay the debts.

The central bank order, which took effect on October 20, says enterprises will be given five days from the notification of a claim by the courts to repay the debt. If the money is not paid, cash can be seized from hard currency accounts.
